meta.paper_title: Aligning Machine and Human Visual Representations

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The pipeline fits a projection head. The split is defined in code (baseline_summary.json 'best node' code and best_solution_*.py): triplets are permuted with np.random.seed(0), n_val=min(20000,len//5) held out as trip_val, the rest trip_train. The projection head is trained on trip_train and OOO accuracy is evaluated on the disjoint trip_val, so the human OOO labels of the eval set are never used during fitting (training matches the SigLIP teacher's pairwise cosine similarities via MSE / (1-cos), not human labels). Baseline (0.4139), teacher (0.4359) and aligned OOO are all computed on trip_val — a genuinely held-out set. Minor hygiene gaps: (a) there is no separate test set — the reported 'best' aligned value 0.4394 (research_summary.json 'Best validation OOO accuracy') is the best epoch selected on the same trip_val that is reported, i.e. model/epoch selection on the eval split; (b) the 1852 THINGS concept images are shared across train/val triplets, which is acceptable for the triplet-OOO protocol. No leakage path materially inflates the conclusion (the effect is ~0). These are small, so above adequate but not perfect.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The ground truth is the human odd-one-out choice column read from the THINGS triplets CSV (triplets_large_final_correctednc_correctedorder.csv), and the metric is OOO accuracy against that human choice — exactly the paper's THINGS Triplet Odd-one-out operationalization (paper Sec 2.1). The label is human-sourced and non-circular (not generated by the model under test). One risk: the choice/index columns are picked by a heuristic find_col() with a fallback to 'first 4 numeric cols', which is not verified against a schema; however the resulting baseline OOO (0.4139) is well above chance (0.333), indicating the columns were mapped correctly. The label validly reflects human similarity structure, with only the unverified column-mapping heuristic as a mild caveat.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: Nominal model/dataset ids match the spec: student = DINOv2 ViT-B (find_model_dir 'dinov2-base'), teacher = SigLIP-So400m (find_model_dir 'siglip-so400m'), dataset = THINGS with 1852 of 1854 concepts and its human triplets (draft_summary.json Description; npy dumps show baseline_ooo=0.4139, teacher_ooo=0.4359 over THINGS). However the single most important specified resource — the TEACHER — is materially downgraded: task.md defines the teacher as 'SigLIP-So400m, the surrogate human-similarity teacher whose image-encoder space is shaped by THINGS triplet judgments' (affine alignment + uncertainty distillation, paper Sec 4.1). The run uses RAW, un-fitted SigLIP features directly; no human-judgment fitting of the teacher was performed. The consequence is measurable: the teacher scores only 43.59% OOO here versus the paper's 61.7% for the properly fitted teacher — confirming the teacher-shaping step was silently skipped. Thus, while the model/dataset ids are honored, the defining transformation that makes the teacher the specified 'human-similarity teacher' was omitted, effectively substituting a different (un-aligned) teacher in the main experiment.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: For the single dimension actually exercised — THINGS OOO alignment (Claim 2 surrogate) — used_n is ample: 20000 held-out validation triplets, full concept set, N_EPOCHS swept over {15,30,50,75}. But 3 of the 4 claims have NO supporting experiment on disk. Grep across every experiment_code.py finds zero references to spearman / ImageNet-A / BREEDS / Birds / UC-Merced / Colon, and npy dumps of all seven experiment_data.npy files contain only OOO accuracy and MSE/cosine losses on THINGS — no ImageNet-triplet synthesis (C1), no Levels/multi-level Spearman (C2 multi-abstraction), no behavioral/uncertainty matching (C3), and no downstream/OOD utility (C4). Yet draft_summary.json Description and plot analyses assert 'one-shot classification on Birds, UC Merced, Colon' and 'ImageNet-A OOD robustness' as if run, and claim 'utility roughly preserved' — conclusions stated without the experiment. This is a substantial evidence-sufficiency shortfall (overclaim on three claims).

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: The code hardcodes torch.manual_seed(42) and np.random.seed(0) with no seed variable, so the framework's four 'best node with different seeds' replicate nodes (experiment_486a, 24c2, f817, 173d) produce BIT-IDENTICAL final aligned OOO values across all runs: {epochs_15:0.4365, 30:0.4355, 50:0.4368, 75:0.4363} in every node. The seed_aggregation_* artifacts therefore report zero genuine variance — the multi-seed aggregation is illusory. No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests accompany the reported numbers, and the headline effect (aligned ~0.437 vs baseline 0.4139, ~2.3 points) is small and plausibly within noise, yet is discussed as a real 'modest ceiling'. This is a single-effective-seed point-estimate regime dressed up with fake seed replication.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The claims are causal ('distilling ... improves', 'alignment is not at odds with utility'), and the run does perform a genuine intervention rather than pure correlation: it trains a distillation projection head and compares the aligned representation against the unaligned baseline (a proper control), plus a loss-function ablation (pairwise-similarity MSE vs direct-feature cosine, ablation_summary.json). This is intervention-based, not correlational-dressed-as-causal. However rigor is weakened: there is no random-direction / random-teacher control, and — most importantly — the very knob the run diagnoses as the cause of the null result, the alignment-loss weight (draft_summary.json: 'alignment loss magnitude ~0.01-0.03 is dwarfed by total loss ~3.25-3.55 ... loss weighting must be recalibrated'), is never swept. So the intervention exists but a key control/sweep is missing.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: The numbers the report.md and draft_summary.json Key_numerical_results actually rely on trace cleanly to on-disk products and agree: baseline 0.4139, teacher 0.4359, aligned best 0.4394 (report says ~0.4397), final alignment loss ~0.012 all match experiment_data.npy contents (verified by loading the .npy files). However the pipeline's narrative artifacts contain numerous SOURCELESS/fabricated figures with no backing product: ablation_summary.json plot_analyses and vlm_feedback_summary report 'Full Model ~0.63 Spearman', 'coarse ~0.70', ''No RSA Loss'/'No KL Loss' variants', '10 downstream datasets', and 'OOD robustness on BREEDS and ImageNet-A improves by 2-5%' — none of which exist in any experiment_data.npy or experiment_code.py (grep confirms no such code ran). The core reported ledger is grounded, but a large volume of auto-generated interpretive numbers are back-filled/hallucinated, so end-to-end traceability is materially incomplete.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: There is a material inconsistency between the pipeline's narrative artifacts and its actual run products. The realized data (all experiment_data.npy) and code compute ONLY THINGS OOO accuracy (~0.436) and MSE/cosine training losses. Yet ablation_summary.json describes an ablation over 'No RSA Loss / No KL Loss / Cosine Only / No Distillation' with 'Full Model ~0.63 Spearman', multi-level coarse/mid/fine correlations, 10-dataset one-shot results, and BREEDS/ImageNet-A robustness — an entirely different, non-existent experiment; and draft_summary.json Description lists Spearman coarse/mid/fine, Birds/UC-Merced/Colon one-shot, and ImageNet-A as if executed. These narratives directly contradict the on-disk products and the actual ablation code (which only swaps pairwise-MSE for direct-feature-cosine, both yielding ~0.436 OOO). The numeric metric tables themselves are internally consistent, but the prose/VLM layers contradict the data, revealing serious bookkeeping/reporting inconsistency.

C1.claim: A teacher model fitted to human triplet-similarity judgments on THINGS captures human similarity structure well enough that, when applied to a large unlabelled image corpus (ImageNet), it can synthesise a large body of human-like similarity judgments spanning multiple abstraction levels.

method.justification: 9a: The method needed for C1 is (i) fitting a teacher to human judgments (affine alignment + uncertainty distillation on THINGS) and (ii) applying it to ImageNet with clustering-based triplet sampling to synthesise pseudo-labels (paper Sec 4.1). The run does NEITHER: it uses raw un-fitted SigLIP features and never touches ImageNet (code/data reference only the 1852 THINGS images). The chosen method is fundamentally misaligned with C1's mechanism — the teacher-fitting and ImageNet-synthesis steps that C1 is entirely about are absent.

experiment.justification: 9b: No experiment tests C1. There is no measurement of teacher fit to human judgments beyond raw-SigLIP OOO on THINGS, and zero ImageNet triplet-synthesis run. The only teacher number produced (43.59% OOO) is from un-fitted SigLIP, not the specified surrogate. The design does not address 'synthesise similarity judgments spanning multiple abstraction levels' at all.

result.justification: 9c: The only relevant on-disk result — raw teacher OOO 43.59% vs the paper's fitted-teacher 61.7% (near the 66.67% ceiling) — shows the (un-fitted) teacher does NOT capture human structure well, contradicting C1; and no ImageNet synthesis result exists. The report does not honestly engage C1 as NOT-REPRODUCED with a reliable reason (report.md merely says 'see overall verdict'), so the claim's surface conclusion is left dangling rather than faithfully judged.

C2.claim: Distilling this human-like similarity structure into pretrained vision foundation models (DINOv2, supervised ViT-L, contrastive image–text models) via a dedicated alignment loss substantially improves their Spearman correlation with human similarity judgments at multiple abstraction levels.

method.justification: 9a: A distillation objective (train a head to match teacher pairwise cosine similarities via MSE; ablation to direct-feature cosine) is a reasonable member of the distillation method family, so the broad approach fits 'distill structure into a student'. But three mismatches lower it: (i) only a projection head on FROZEN DINOv2 features is trained, not the finetuning of the backbone the paper uses; (ii) the teacher supplying the target is un-fitted raw SigLIP, so the distilled signal is not the 'human-like similarity structure' the claim specifies; (iii) only DINOv2 is used, and the metric is OOO accuracy, not Spearman 'at multiple abstraction levels'. Broadly the right family but materially off-target.

experiment.justification: 9b: The design includes a baseline-vs-aligned control, an N_EPOCHS sweep, and a loss-type ablation — honest but under-powered. The judgment metric (single-facet OOO accuracy on THINGS) does not correspond to the claim's 'Spearman correlation at multiple abstraction levels' (no Levels / coarse-mid-fine Spearman was computed). Critically, the one hyperparameter the run itself identifies as decisive — the alignment-loss weight — is never swept, so a true negative cannot be distinguished from under-exploration. Multi-seed replication is illusory (identical hardcoded seeds).

result.justification: 9c: The grounded result — aligned 0.437 vs baseline 0.4139 (~+2 pts, within noise) — is honestly summarised in report.md/draft_summary.json as 'essentially no measurable improvement', which qualitatively DISAGREES with the paper's substantial gains (21.28–74.47% relative on THINGS). The honest direction is credible, but it is an under-explored null (un-fitted teacher, frozen-backbone head, un-swept loss weight) rather than a clean can't-reproduce, and — worse — the ablation_summary.json narrative fabricates agreement ('all alignment variants exceed baseline', 'Full Model ~0.63') that contradicts the data. The honest ledger pulls this up from a 1; the fabricated narrative and under-exploration keep it low.

C3.claim: After alignment, the fine-tuned student models more accurately reproduce human behavioural patterns and uncertainty on similarity tasks than their unaligned counterparts.

method.justification: 9a: C3 requires modelling human behavioural patterns and uncertainty (e.g. correlating model uncertainty / triplet entropy with human response times, RSA behaviour matching, per the paper Fig 2e). No such method is implemented anywhere — no entropy-vs-RT analysis, no RSA, no behavioural-distribution matching. The method needed for the claim is entirely absent.

experiment.justification: 9b: No experiment measures behavioural/uncertainty reproduction. The only on-disk products are OOO accuracy and training losses; a pred-vs-gt histogram exists but does not test uncertainty calibration against human response times. The claim is not exercised.

result.justification: 9c: No result addressing behavioural/uncertainty matching exists; report.md gives only a generic 'see overall verdict'. Auto-generated narratives mention RSA/uncertainty but with no backing data. The claim is left unjudged, neither reproduced nor honestly reported as non-reproduced.

C4.claim: Alignment is not at odds with utility: aligned student models match or exceed the originals on diverse downstream tasks and improve out-of-distribution robustness.

method.justification: 9a: C4 requires downstream one-shot classification evaluation and OOD/robustness evaluation (BREEDS, ImageNet-A). Grep across all experiment_code.py finds no downstream/robustness code, and no experiment_data.npy contains any such metric — the method for testing utility/OOD is absent. draft_summary.json claims one-shot on Birds/UC-Merced/Colon and ImageNet-A were part of the pipeline, but no code or data supports this.

experiment.justification: 9b: No downstream, BREEDS, or ImageNet-A experiment was run (verified: zero matching keys in any npy, zero references in any experiment_code.py). The experimental design for the utility/robustness claim does not exist.

result.justification: 9c: The report/summary asserts 'utility is roughly preserved' and the ablation narrative fabricates 'OOD robustness on BREEDS and ImageNet-A improves by 2-5%' — conclusions stated with no experiment run and no backing product (fabrication/overclaim). This disguises absence of evidence as support, the worst-case result-analysis failure.
